new_candidates.legal_basis: 12-month moratorium approved by County Board vote 2026-05-19; declared invalid by Logan County State's Attorney Bradley Hauge on 2026-06-18 because it was not referred to the Zoning Board of Appeals for advisory review or subjected to public hearings before final passage, as required by county procedure.
new_candidates.trigger: Response to Hut 8 Corp.'s proposed ~500 MW 'Logan Prairie' data center near Latham; residents sought time to study the project and adopt safeguards before the county acted on Hut 8's land-use application.
new_candidates.current_status: Not currently in force as of 2026-09-23. The May 19, 2026 moratorium was ruled procedurally invalid on 2026-06-18, and the State's Attorney directed the zoning office to accept Hut 8's rezoning application (deemed complete June 29, 2026); Hut 8 has since filed a further rezoning application for a 720-acre site. As of Aug. 4, 2026, the Board's Zoning and Economic Development Committee was drafting a replacement moratorium (targeting data centers over 100 MW) and submitted it to the State's Attorney for review, but no adoption had been reported by Sept. 17-18, 2026; that most recent reporting instead describes the Board advancing 18 amendments to its permanent data-center zoning ordinance (height cap, setbacks, a faster environmental-discharge cure period), separate from any new moratorium.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Hut 8 Corp.'s proposed 'Logan Prairie Data Center' (~500 MW, originally on ~250 acres, later refiled for 720 acres) near Latham, IL; a ~$5B project. Hut 8 has also been in talks with the Village of Latham about possible annexation, which could remove the site from county zoning jurisdiction.
new_candidates.outcome: The county's attempt to pause data-center applications while it developed permanent zoning was defeated on procedural grounds; as of this research pass the county had not re-adopted a valid moratorium and was instead pursuing amendments to a permanent data-center zoning ordinance while Hut 8's rezoning application proceeds.

evidence.title: Data center moratorium declared invalid
evidence.supports: Details the May 19, 2026 6-4 vote adopting a 12-month moratorium, and the State's Attorney's June 18, 2026 ruling that it was procedurally invalid because it skipped the Zoning Board of Appeals advisory step and public hearings.
evidence.quote: State's Attorney Bradley Hauge advised County Board members during a closed-door meeting June 18 and before the board meeting that same day that proper procedures weren't followed for the moratorium to be legally binding... Hauge said he advised the county's zoning office to accept Hut 8's land-use application...

evidence.title: Logan County committee reevaluates data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Confirms the Zoning and Economic Development Committee's Aug. 4, 2026 agreement to submit a draft replacement moratorium (targeting data centers over 100 MW) to the State's Attorney for review, and recaps the Feb. 24 60-day and May 19 12-month moratorium history.
evidence.quote: LINCOLN — After their first effort was declared invalid, Logan County Board members are revisiting the imposition of a 12-month moratorium on large scale data centers. On Monday, its Zoning and Economic Development Committee agreed to submit a draft moratorium to Logan County State's Attorney Brad Hauge...

evidence.title: Central Illinois counties advance data center regulations
evidence.supports: Sept. 17-18, 2026 reporting shows Logan County's Zoning and Economic Development Committee advancing 18 amendments to its permanent data-center zoning ordinance (not a new moratorium vote), and that Hut 8 has filed a further rezoning application for 720 acres.
evidence.quote: The Logan County Zoning and Economic Development Committee held a special meeting Thursday to submit 18 amendments to the county's zoning ordinance regulating data centers... Although Hut 8... filed another rezoning application in Logan County for a 500-megawatt data center near Latham...

new_candidates.notes: enacted_status is recorded as 'rescinded' as the closest codebook fit for a moratorium that was adopted but then ruled legally invalid/unenforceable on procedural grounds (rather than a term expiring or a deliberate repeal vote). Status is unusually complex and worth a dedicated follow-up: as of 2026-09-23 there is no indication a new, procedurally valid moratorium has been adopted, even though the county continues to describe itself as having 'issued multiple moratoriums.'

new_candidates.duration: A solar-farm (and later wind/solar) moratorium was repeatedly extended by the Catlin Village Board in roughly 30-day increments during 2026 while the village drafted a permanent solar/wind zoning ordinance (exact original enactment date not found); most recently extended to Aug. 31, 2026. It was superseded by the permanent ordinance in late August 2026.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Catlin Village Board resolution(s)/motions repeatedly extending a solar-farm moratorium (specific instrument numbers not found); superseded by a permanent wind-and-solar zoning ordinance approved in late August 2026.
new_candidates.trigger: Earthrise Energy's proposed 1,400-acre solar-farm project along Catlin-Tilton Road; the village wanted time to draft zoning language addressing setbacks, screening, and water testing for industrial-scale solar and wind projects before acting on the application.
new_candidates.current_status: Replaced as of late August 2026. The Village Council approved a permanent wind-and-solar zoning ordinance in the days before Sept. 1, 2026, after which companies (including Earthrise) could begin submitting special-use permit applications for wind and solar projects, ending the moratorium.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Earthrise Energy's proposed 1,400-acre solar farm along Catlin-Tilton Road (Tilton Solar project).
new_candidates.outcome: The moratorium was replaced by a permanent solar/wind zoning ordinance approved by the Village Council in late August 2026, which now governs special-use applications for wind and solar projects (including annual water testing for private wells within 500 feet of a project boundary).

evidence.title: Catlin extends its solar-farm moratorium to Aug. 31
evidence.supports: Confirms the village repeatedly extended a solar-farm moratorium (most recently to Aug. 31, 2026) while drafting zoning-ordinance changes, in the context of Earthrise Energy's pending 1,400-acre solar farm application.
evidence.quote: the Catlin Village Board extended its solar-farm moratorium again Tuesday night to Aug. 31... Village officials said they think another 30 days should be enough time as they continue to work with a specialized Springfield attorney on the zoning-ordinance changes.

evidence.title: Catlin approves solar, wind ordinance
evidence.supports: Confirms the village council approved a permanent wind-and-solar ordinance in late August 2026, after which companies could submit special-use permit applications, ending the moratorium.
evidence.quote: Late last week, the village council approved a wind and solar ordinance to regulate such projects, including Earthrise Energy's proposal for a 1,400-acre solar-farm project along Catlin-Tilton Road... Starting today, Catlin Mayor Justin Bargo said, companies can submit special-use permit applications for wind and solar projects...

new_candidates.notes: Original enactment date of the underlying moratorium could not be pinned down this pass (one resident described the overall dispute as running 'the last year and a half to two years'); included as 'replaced' for completeness since the instrument was explicitly called a moratorium and has now fully run its course.

new_candidates.duration: The Robinson City Council voted to extend an existing solar-farm moratorium for another six months (article published 2026-09-08); original enactment date not found.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Robinson City Council ordinance/motion extending a moratorium on solar-farm development (specific instrument number not found)
new_candidates.trigger: Uncertainty over which level of government (city, county, or state) has zoning jurisdiction over solar farms in the area surrounding Robinson; aldermen wanted to wait until that question is resolved.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23 per the most recent extension reported.
new_candidates.outcome: Continues the ban on new solar farms in and around the city while jurisdictional questions with the state/county are resolved.

evidence.title: Robinson solar farm moratorium extended
evidence.supports: Confirms the city council's vote to extend the solar-farm moratorium (covering the city and the area within 1.5 miles of its corporate limits) for another six months.
evidence.quote: The Robinson City Council has voted to extend for another six months a moratorium on solar farms. The moratorium covers the city and the area within a mile-and-a-half of its corporate limits... Aldermen decided it was best to extend the moratorium until the matter is resolved.

new_candidates.notes: Original adoption date of the underlying moratorium was not found this pass; confidence lowered accordingly. Worth a follow-up search of Robinson's city council minutes/ordinances for the original instrument.

new_candidates.date_enacted: Original 180-day moratorium established by City Council ordinance on approximately 2026-03-03; unanimously extended by the City Council on 2026-08-18 through August 25, 2027.
new_candidates.duration: Moratorium on data centers in all zoning districts within the city; originally 180 days from March 2026, unanimously extended on 2026-08-18 to run through August 25, 2027, citing continued state inaction on the POWER Act.
new_candidates.legal_basis: City of Ottawa ordinance establishing and later extending a data center moratorium (specific ordinance numbers not published in sources reviewed)
new_candidates.trigger: State inaction on the POWER Act, which would set energy/water guidelines for data centers; the city has been drafting its own data-center ordinance but wants to wait until the state acts so local rules align with state law.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; extended through August 25, 2027.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None specified; no official plans for large-scale data centers in the area were reported.
new_candidates.outcome: City continues drafting its own data-center ordinance but is waiting for state legislative action (the POWER Act) before adopting it, extending the moratorium in the meantime.

evidence.title: Ottawa extends data center moratorium through August 2027
evidence.supports: Confirms the city council's unanimous vote extending its data-center moratorium through Aug. 25, 2027, and that it applies to all zoning districts.
evidence.quote: Ottawa extended its temporary moratorium on data centers in all zoning districts until August 2027... The city council unanimously passed the ordinance Tuesday night... The moratorium applies to all zoning districts within the city and remains in effect through Aug. 25, 2027.

new_candidates.notes: Original enactment date (~March 2026) taken from a third-party tracker (SAVRN), which was not independently verified against a primary Ottawa source this pass; the extension itself is well-sourced. date_enacted_uncertainty set to month_only to reflect the imprecise original date.

new_candidates.date_enacted: Rockford City Council voted 14-0 to approve the moratorium at its Monday, 2026-08-03 meeting.
new_candidates.duration: Six-month moratorium on data centers, directing city staff to conduct a comprehensive review of best practices for data center development, expansion, and operation.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Rockford City Council ordinance/resolution establishing a six-month data center moratorium and staff review (specific instrument number not published in sources reviewed), brought forward by Alderman Jonathan Logemann
new_candidates.trigger: Sustained resident opposition at council meetings to a potential hyperscale data center development (Monarch Energy) citing energy demand, water consumption, noise, and environmental effects.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. Explicitly does not apply to the Edson Road land where Monarch Energy has been pursuing a data center, because that land is already covered by an existing annexation agreement permitting data center development that cannot be changed without both parties' consent.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Excludes (does not apply to) the Edson Road parcel Monarch Energy is pursuing for a hyperscale data center; no formal Monarch Energy proposal had been submitted as of adoption.
new_candidates.outcome: Pauses data center development citywide (outside the Edson Road exemption) while staff develop best-practices policy recommendations.

evidence.title: Rockford approves data center moratorium, but not for Monarch's land
evidence.supports: Confirms the 14-0 vote, the six-month term, the exemption for the Monarch Energy Edson Road land, and the rationale.
evidence.quote: Aldermen voted 14-0 on Monday to approve the moratorium and direct city staff to conduct a comprehensive review of the best practices regarding the development, expansion and operation of data centers... City Administrator Todd Cagnoni said the moratorium doesn't apply to land along Edson Road where Monarch Energy has been pursuing a data center.

new_candidates.date_enacted: Woodford County Board approved the moratorium at its Aug. 18, 2026 meeting, after weeks of discussion.
new_candidates.duration: Six-month moratorium on data center applications, with an option for the Board to extend it another six months; the initial term runs through approximately February 2027 while the county holds public hearings and develops a data-center ordinance.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Woodford County Board ordinance/resolution establishing a six-month data center moratorium with a one-time six-month extension option (specific instrument number not published in sources reviewed)
new_candidates.trigger: County wanted time to develop transparent data-center regulations and hold public hearings, comparing its approach to how it previously handled large wind and solar developments.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. No future dates for further ordinance discussion had been announced as of the Aug. 21, 2026 report.
new_candidates.outcome: Pause while the county studies data-center land-use, economic, and infrastructure implications and develops a transparent, case-by-case regulatory process.

evidence.title: Tazewell County revisits data center ordinance, Woodford County passes moratorium
evidence.supports: Confirms the Woodford County Board approved a six-month moratorium with a six-month extension option, running through February 2027, following weeks of discussion.
evidence.quote: In Woodford County, after weeks of discussion, the County Board approved a six-month moratorium on data center applications, with an option for a six-month extension. The initial moratorium would run through February 2027 while the county holds public hearings and develops a data center ordinance.

new_candidates.notes: Exact Aug. 18, 2026 date taken from the third-party SAVRN tracker, consistent with the 'February 2027' end date reported by 25 News/WMBD; not independently confirmed against a Woodford County primary source this pass.

new_candidates.date_enacted: Plainfield Village Board voted unanimously to pass the moratorium ordinance; reported by Patch on 2026-04-21 as a Monday-night vote (i.e., on or about 2026-04-20/21).
new_candidates.duration: 180-day moratorium on the receipt, processing, approval, and permitting of applications for data centers and warehouses primarily used for storing computing infrastructure.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Village of Plainfield ordinance establishing a 180-day moratorium on data centers and computing-infrastructure warehouses (specific ordinance number not published in sources reviewed)
new_candidates.trigger: Concern over rapid data-center development converting valuable farmland in nearby towns (Joliet, Yorkville, Minooka); the Mayor said the industry is 'in its infancy' and the village wants time to develop a new unified development ordinance addressing data centers.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; original term runs through approximately October 18, 2026. The Mayor said in April 2026 it was 'highly likely' the moratorium would be extended multiple times before the village reaches regulatory clarity.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named; several nearby communities (Joliet, Yorkville, Minooka) have already approved data centers.
new_candidates.outcome: Pause to allow staff, elected officials, and consultants to study best practices and develop a new unified development ordinance addressing data centers.

evidence.title: Data Center Moratorium Imposed In Plainfield After Unanimous Village Board Vote
evidence.supports: Confirms the unanimous Village Board vote for a 180-day moratorium on data centers and warehouses, and quotes the Mayor on the rationale and likelihood of extension.
evidence.quote: PLAINFIELD, IL — The Plainfield Village Board unanimously voted Monday night to pass a 180-day moratorium on data centers and warehouses... The mayor said it's 'highly likely' the 180-day moratorium will be extended multiple times.

new_candidates.notes: This moratorium's original 180-day term (through roughly Oct. 18, 2026) is about to run out; given the Mayor's stated expectation of extension, a near-term follow-up check for an extension vote is warranted but was outside the scope of this pass since it had not yet occurred as of 2026-09-23.

new_candidates.date_enacted: Lawrence County Board voted unanimously on Thursday, 2026-09-17 to approve the moratorium ordinance.
new_candidates.duration: Two-year moratorium on data centers exceeding 10,000 square feet; the county will not accept applications for such facilities while it is in effect.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Lawrence County Board ordinance establishing a two-year data center moratorium (specific ordinance number not published in sources reviewed); modeled on a similar moratorium enacted in neighboring Crawford County, Illinois, with the two counties' State's Attorneys collaborating on the ordinance language.
new_candidates.trigger: Board wanted time to educate itself and residents on the problems and benefits of data centers before allowing development; public testimony (including from residents of neighboring Sullivan County, Indiana and Crawford County, Illinois describing negative experiences with nearby data center development) influenced the decision.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named; described as a preemptive, county-wide pause rather than a response to a specific proposal.
new_candidates.outcome: Two-year pause intended to let the board and public study data-center impacts, infrastructure demands, and community effects before any project proceeds.

evidence.title: Lawrence Co., IL board enacts two-year moratorium on data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the Thursday (Sept. 17, 2026) unanimous vote and the two-year term applying to data centers of at least 10,000 square feet.
evidence.quote: The Lawrence County, Illinois Board voted Thursday to approve an ordinance for a two-year moratorium on data centers. It also stipulates that any application submitted to the county for a data center at least 10,000 square feet in size will not be accepted.

evidence.title: There Are No Data Centers in Lawrence County... For The Next Two Years
evidence.supports: Independent corroborating source with additional detail: the ordinance was modeled after a moratorium in neighboring Crawford County, Illinois, and quotes the Board Chairman and a Board member on the rationale.
evidence.quote: County officials modeled the ordinance after a similar moratorium enacted in neighboring Crawford County. Lawrence County State's Attorney Brady Waldrop worked alongside Crawford County State's Attorney Cole Shaner to draft the language.

new_candidates.notes: Sources reference a similar, apparently pre-existing data-center moratorium in neighboring Crawford County, Illinois, which was not independently verified or added as its own candidate this pass due to time constraints; flagging for a future research pass.
